# Company 057 — Fraud Detection API

**Company ID:** `company:future:057`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:057`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-057-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer blocking, payment denial, account suspension or fraud accusation.

## Business identity

Purpose: provide real-time and batch risk scoring for suspicious transactions, signups, account activity, promotions, marketplace behavior, returns and identity/device patterns.

Problem: fraud signals are distributed across accounts, devices, transactions and behavior; simplistic rules create false positives while adaptive attackers exploit gaps.

Value: explainable risk scores, reusable signals, graph intelligence and policy-ready decisions while leaving irreversible enforcement behind explicit customer policy/authorization.

## Complete product tree

Transaction Risk API; Signup Risk API; Account-Takeover Detection; Device/Session Risk; Promotion/Abuse Detection; Bot/Automation Detection; Marketplace Fraud; Returns/Refund Abuse; Chargeback Risk; Identity/Entity Risk; Graph Risk Engine; Velocity Rules; Behavioral Anomaly Engine; Watchlist/Policy Rules; Case Management; Feedback/Labeling; Fraud Analytics; Simulation/Backtesting; Decision API; SDKs; Edge/Streaming Scoring; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical Fraud Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: identity/device/session/payment/account/entity features, IP/network context, velocity, geolocation consistency, graph relationships, behavioral sequences, transaction amount/currency, merchant/product/channel, historical outcomes, rule hits, model scores, confidence, reason codes, thresholds, challenge/review recommendations, feedback labels, drift and false-positive analysis.

Customers: ecommerce, fintech infrastructure, marketplaces, SaaS, subscription businesses, gaming, ticketing, delivery, travel, digital goods, loyalty/promotion programs, enterprise security teams and platform developers.

Verticals: payments/commerce, account security, marketplaces, digital content, travel, ticketing, gaming, subscriptions, advertising/promo systems. Each requires separate fraud taxonomies, labels and regulation/policy boundaries.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may analyze cases, synthesize evidence and recommend investigations. Core scoring should combine deterministic rules, graph algorithms, statistical/ML models and calibrated confidence. LLMs may summarize evidence but must not be sole fraud classifiers for high-impact decisions.

Architecture: low-latency feature service, event stream, identity/device/entity graph, rules engine, model registry/router, scoring service, case store, feedback labels, drift monitoring, simulation/backtest, privacy controls, decision policy adapter and audit/provenance.

## Agent tree

Signal Collector; Identity/Device Agent; Graph Analyst; Behavioral Analyst; Transaction Risk Agent; Promotion Abuse Agent; Case Investigator; Rule/Model QA Agent; Drift Agent; Feedback/Label Agent; Fraud Operations Assistant; Incident/Security Agent.

## Deterministic services

Feature extraction; velocity counters; graph traversal; duplicate/entity resolution; rule evaluation; thresholding; model serving; calibration; reason-code mapping; rate limiting; idempotency; streaming/batch scoring; feedback ingestion; retention; protected enforcement hooks.

## Workflow tree

Event/request → authenticate tenant → collect/derive allowed features → evaluate rules/graph/models → combine/calibrate score → produce reason codes + recommended action class → customer policy chooses allow/challenge/review/block → enforcement only through customer-authorized system → outcome/chargeback/appeal feedback → model/rule monitoring and retraining governance.

## Integrations / API / data

Payments, ecommerce, identity/auth, device intelligence, account systems, marketplace/order platforms, chargeback/returns systems, support/case management, data warehouses and event streams. APIs for score, batch score, features, cases, labels, rules, models and analytics.

Data: events, identities, devices, accounts, transactions, relationships, scores, rule hits, outcomes, appeals and labels. Sensitive personal/financial data requires minimization, jurisdiction controls and isolation.

## Monetization / distribution

Per API call/event, monthly active users/accounts, transactions, feature volume, enterprise/private, premium graph/device packs, case seats, managed fraud ops. Distribution through payment/ecommerce/identity marketplaces and developer/fintech ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance

High-impact decisions require explainability, appeal/human review options where applicable, bias/fairness testing, privacy minimization and strict secret/tenant isolation. Do not label people criminals; score behavior/risk under customer policy. Regional consumer/financial rules must be respected.

## Failure / edge cases

New-user cold start, shared household/device, VPN/proxy, travel, accessibility automation, high-value legitimate purchase, synthetic identity, mule networks, coordinated marketplace rings, bot adaptation, feedback poisoning, label delay, concept drift, sparse data, provider outage. False-positive/false-negative tradeoffs must be explicit.

## Scale / overlap

Single API → multi-signal fraud platform → real-time risk infrastructure. Overlap #44 chargeback recovery, #57 owns detection/scoring, #66 AI runtime security, #91 identity/trust authority. Fraud-company data cannot casually feed other projects.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** event identity, tenant isolation, confidence/reason codes, policy-vs-score separation, feedback/evaluation, privacy and model versioning.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center risk/security engines should preserve generic scoring/evidence hooks without importing customer fraud data.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** low-latency feature/rules/model serving, graph, drift/evaluation and case infrastructure.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** fraud models, data providers, vertical packs, customer enforcement connectors, pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global graph/stream infrastructure and privacy-safe consortium signals.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: transaction/signup/ATO/device/promo/bot/marketplace/returns/chargeback/identity/graph/rules/behavior/cases/analytics/backtest/API.
2. Feature Tree: identity/device/network/velocity/graph/behavior/transaction/history/model/reasons/thresholds/feedback/drift.
3. Customer Tree: ecommerce/fintech/marketplace/SaaS/gaming/ticketing/delivery/travel/digital/subscription/enterprise.
4. Vertical Tree: payments/commerce/accounts/marketplaces/content/travel/tickets/gaming/subscriptions/promotions.
5. Brain Tree: evidence/case analysis; core scoring uses calibrated rules/graph/ML, not unsupported LLM judgment.
6. Agent Tree: signals/identity/graph/behavior/transaction/promo/case/QA/drift/feedback/ops/security.
7. Service Tree: features/velocity/graph/entity/rules/model/calibration/reasons/rate limit/idempotency/feedback.
8. Workflow Tree: event→features→score→reasons→policy decision→authorized enforcement→outcome feedback→monitor.
9. Integration Tree: payments/commerce/auth/device/account/marketplace/chargeback/returns/support/warehouse/streams.
10. Data Tree: events/identities/devices/accounts/transactions/relations/scores/outcomes/appeals/labels.
11. API Tree: score/batch/features/cases/labels/rules/models/analytics.
12. Monetization Tree: calls/events/MAU/transactions/features/enterprise/case seats/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: payments/ecommerce/identity marketplaces/developer/fintech partners.
14. Automation Tree: scoring/monitoring automated; high-impact enforcement remains customer-policy controlled.
15. Moat Tree: labeled outcomes, graph intelligence, calibrated models, vertical fraud packs, integration breadth.
16. Platform Tree: scoring API→fraud OS→real-time trust/risk infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: bias/false positives/privacy leak/model drift/feedback poisoning/attacker adaptation.
18. Scale Tree: API→platform→global streaming graph.
19. Spinoff Tree: device intelligence/graph risk may become modules; identity/trust and chargeback products remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: model/evaluation registry, privacy, risk policy, event bus, low-latency APIs, isolation, observability.
21. Design-Now Requirements: calibrated-score/reason/evidence/policy-separation and model-version interfaces.
22. Build-Now Requirements: preserve reusable risk-scoring/evaluation hooks in shared security/Brain infrastructure.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: fraud datasets/models/provider connectors/customer enforcement/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: signals/models/rules monitor and score continuously; humans focus on novel rings, appeals and policy changes.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into identity/trust, runtime security, chargeback or specialized abuse modules already represented elsewhere.

# Company 058 — Employee Onboarding / Offboarding Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:058`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:058`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-058-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no employee account creation, permission change, payroll change, termination action or external communication.

## Business identity

Purpose: coordinate employee/contractor lifecycle tasks across HR, IT, security, payroll, facilities, training and managers with explicit authority, evidence and rapid revocation on departure.

Problem: onboarding/offboarding spans many systems and human owners; missed tasks create productivity delays, orphaned access, equipment loss and security/compliance gaps.

Value: one durable lifecycle workflow, least-privilege access plans, exact task ownership, verified completion and safe termination containment.

## Complete product tree

New-Hire Intake; Role/Access Plan; Account Provisioning Orchestrator; Equipment/Asset Workflow; Payroll/Benefits Checklist Adapter; Policy/Acknowledgment; Training/Certification; Manager Checklist; Facilities/Badge Workflow; Contractor Lifecycle; Transfer/Role-Change Workflow; Leave/Suspension Workflow; Offboarding; Access Revocation; Asset Return; Knowledge Handoff; Exit Evidence Pack; Lifecycle Analytics; API/SDK; HRIS/ITSM/IAM Integrations; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Industry Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: person/worker identity, employment type, start/end dates, department/manager/location, role template, system access, group/role membership, equipment, policies, training, approvals, payroll/benefits handoffs, exceptions, termination urgency, revocation timestamps, asset return, shared-secret rotation triggers, audit and retention.

Customers: SMBs, enterprises, IT/HR/security teams, MSPs, staffing companies, distributed/remote companies, regulated organizations and franchises.

Verticals: technology, professional services, healthcare administration, finance-adjacent organizations, retail, hospitality, manufacturing, education, nonprofits and government. Packs vary by identity/compliance/equipment/training requirements.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may interpret role/job information, recommend access/equipment/training templates, detect missing steps and summarize exceptions. Deterministic HR/IAM policy owns authorization. Brain cannot grant privilege, alter payroll or terminate employment independently.

Architecture: worker identity registry, lifecycle state machine, role/access templates, system connector registry, task DAG, asset registry, policy/training records, approval engine, credential rotation hooks, audit/evidence ledger and protected account/communication actions.

## Agent tree

Lifecycle Coordinator; HR Data Agent; Access Planner; IAM Provisioning Agent; Equipment Agent; Training Agent; Policy Acknowledgment Agent; Manager Coordinator; Contractor Agent; Offboarding/Revoke Agent; Asset Return Agent; Knowledge-Handoff Agent; QA/Security Agent.

## Deterministic services

Identity linking; lifecycle dates; role/access matrix; approval rules; task scheduler; provisioning/deprovisioning adapters; group/role diff; asset custody; acknowledgment records; revoke-all workflow; idempotency; evidence; emergency kill switch.

## Workflow tree

Authorized lifecycle event → verify worker/role/date → build tasks/access plan → obtain approvals → provision accounts/equipment/training → verify each result → active lifecycle monitoring/changes → transfer/leave/offboarding event → freeze new privilege → revoke/disable at correct time → recover assets/rotate shared credentials → verify downstream removal → close with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

HRIS, IAM/SSO, SaaS directories, cloud, email/collaboration, payroll/benefits handoff, ITSM, MDM/device inventory, badge/access, training/LMS, asset systems, ticketing. APIs for workers, lifecycle events, access plans, tasks, assets, acknowledgments and evidence.

Data: worker identities, roles, employment state, access assignments, approvals, tasks, assets, training, policy acknowledgments, revocations and evidence. Highly sensitive HR/security data remains isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Employees/contractors, connected systems, lifecycle events, seats, enterprise/private, MSP/multi-client, premium compliance packs, API/OEM, managed operations. Distribution via HRIS/IAM/ITSM marketplaces, MSPs and HR/IT/security partners.

## Security/privacy/compliance

High identity/privacy impact. Least privilege, separation of duties, manager/HR authority, time-bound access, termination emergency path, no employment decision making by AI, audit, data minimization and retention controls.

## Failure / edge cases

Rehire, same-name identities, contractor-to-employee conversion, delayed termination, legal hold, shared account, unavailable HRIS, provisioning succeeds but callback fails, transfer across entities, leave of absence, device not returned, departed admin owns integrations, emergency suspension. Idempotency and reconciliation are mandatory.

## Scale / overlap

Small business checklist → enterprise identity lifecycle → workforce access orchestration. Overlap #62 credentialing, #73 credential rotation, #74 permission optimization, #75 access review. #058 owns employment lifecycle orchestration.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** identity lifecycle, time-bound authority, task DAG, connector/reconciliation, emergency revocation, evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center identity/Agency/account-isolation models should preserve actor lifecycle and revocation hooks.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** HR/IAM connector abstractions, role templates, asset/task registries and reconciliation.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** HR/payroll/device connectors, customer UI, industry packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global workforce entities, complex multi-organization federation.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: intake/access/equipment/payroll handoff/policy/training/manager/facilities/contractor/transfer/leave/offboard/revoke/assets/handoff/analytics/API.
2. Feature Tree: identity/type/dates/manager/location/role/access/assets/policies/training/approvals/revocation/audit.
3. Customer Tree: SMB/enterprise/HR/IT/security/MSP/staffing/remote/regulated/franchise.
4. Vertical Tree: tech/services/health admin/finance-adjacent/retail/hospitality/manufacturing/education/government.
5. Brain Tree: template/exception recommendations; privilege/payroll/employment decisions prohibited without authority.
6. Agent Tree: lifecycle/HR/access/IAM/equipment/training/policy/manager/contractor/revoke/assets/handoff/QA.
7. Service Tree: identity/lifecycle/role matrix/approvals/scheduler/connectors/assets/acknowledgments/idempotency/revoke-all.
8. Workflow Tree: event→plan→approve→provision→verify→monitor→offboard/revoke→reconcile→evidence.
9. Integration Tree: HRIS/IAM/SaaS/cloud/email/payroll/ITSM/MDM/badge/LMS/assets/tickets.
10. Data Tree: workers/roles/access/approvals/tasks/assets/training/policy/revocations/evidence.
11. API Tree: workers/events/access plans/tasks/assets/acknowledgments/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: workers/systems/events/seats/enterprise/MSP/API/managed/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: HRIS/IAM/ITSM marketplaces/MSPs/HR-IT-security partners.
14. Automation Tree: task/provision/revoke/reconcile automated within policy; employment/privilege authority gated.
15. Moat Tree: connector breadth, lifecycle templates, reconciliation accuracy, exception patterns.
16. Platform Tree: lifecycle checklist→identity automation→workforce access control plane.
17. Risk Tree: orphaned privilege/wrong person/early termination/privacy leak/failed revoke/asset loss.
18. Scale Tree: SMB→enterprise→global multi-entity workforce.
19. Spinoff Tree: access planner/asset lifecycle modules; permission/access review remain separate companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: identity, authorization, connectors, tasks, devices/assets, audit, incidents, secrets.
21. Design-Now Requirements: durable actor lifecycle and global revocation/reconciliation seams.
22. Build-Now Requirements: preserve identity/session/account lifecycle hooks across Command Center services.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: HR/payroll/device connectors/customer UI/packs/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: routine onboarding/transfers/offboarding execute as verified workflows; humans authorize employment/privilege exceptions and sensitive decisions.

# Company 059 — Marketplace Listing Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:059`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:059`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-059-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no marketplace listing publication, price/inventory change or account mutation.

## Business identity

Purpose: convert canonical product truth into compliant, optimized and synchronized listings across marketplaces while detecting channel errors, suppressions and drift.

Problem: each marketplace has unique taxonomy, attributes, images, titles, policies, inventory/pricing interfaces and error states; manual synchronization creates stale or suppressed listings.

Value: faster channel expansion, fewer listing errors, consistent product identity, auditable changes and channel-specific optimization without corrupting canonical catalog data.

## Complete product tree

Marketplace Connector Hub; Listing Builder; Taxonomy/Attribute Mapper; Title/Description Optimizer; Image/Media Packager; Variant/Parent-Child Mapper; Inventory Sync; Price/Promotion Sync Adapter; Compliance/Restricted-Product Checker; Listing Health Monitor; Suppression/Error Resolver; Feed Submission Manager; Localization; Review/Content Policy Assistant; Channel Analytics; Bulk Operations; Template/Rules Library; API/SDK; Agency/Multi-Client Edition; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Marketplace/Vertical Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: source product/version, channel listing ID, taxonomy/category, attributes, variations, title/bullets/description, search terms, media, dimensions, shipping fields, compliance fields, price/inventory references, eligibility, submission status, warnings/errors/suppressions, channel-specific overrides, approval history, publish version and reconciliation.

Customers: marketplace sellers, ecommerce brands, manufacturers, distributors, agencies, aggregators, multi-brand operators, retailers, PIM vendors and enterprise commerce teams.

Verticals: apparel, beauty, home, automotive, electronics, grocery, pet, industrial, books/media, jewelry and regulated/restricted categories. Each marketplace/category requires policy/attribute packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may recommend channel copy, taxonomy mappings and error resolution based on approved source data. Deterministic validators own required fields, product identity, variant consistency, restricted-category policy and exact feed structure. Brain cannot invent regulated claims or publish without protected authority.

Architecture: canonical catalog adapter, marketplace schema registry, mapping/rules engine, listing version store, content generator with provenance, media transformer, submission queue, inventory/price adapters, error/suppression parser, reconciliation service, policy packs and protected publishing gate.

## Agent tree

Channel Mapping Agent; Listing Copy Agent; Media Agent; Variant Agent; Compliance Agent; Feed Submission Planner; Error/Suppression Agent; Inventory Sync Agent; Price Sync Agent; Localization Agent; Analytics Agent; Reconciliation Agent; Listing QA Agent.

## Deterministic services

Channel schemas; taxonomy maps; attribute validators; variant constraints; feed serializer; media specs; rate limits; idempotent submission; listing version/hash; inventory reservation interface; price/inventory authority boundaries; error code registry; retry/backoff; reconciliation.

## Workflow tree

Select canonical product version → choose channel/category → map taxonomy/attributes/variants → generate permitted channel content/media → validate compliance/required fields → review overrides → create exact listing package/version → protected publish → parse channel response → resolve errors/suppressions → reconcile channel listing ID/state → monitor drift/inventory/price feeds → update only from newer canonical state.

## Integrations / API / data

PIM/catalog, ecommerce platforms, marketplaces, DAM/media, inventory/OMS, pricing, shipping, compliance/product data, localization and analytics. APIs for listings, mappings, validation, feeds, submission status, channel errors and reconciliation.

Data: channel accounts/refs, product versions, mapping rules, listing packages, media refs, publication versions, channel IDs, errors, suppression states, inventory/price sync status and evidence. Account credentials remain secret references only.

## Monetization / distribution

Listings/SKUs, marketplaces/channels, feed volume, locations/accounts, seats, agency clients, API usage, enterprise/private, premium channel/vertical packs and managed listing operations. Distribution via ecommerce/PIM/agency ecosystems and marketplace app stores where allowed.

## Security/privacy/compliance

# Company 060 — Software Migration Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:060`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:060`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-060-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer cutover, data mutation, credential use, migration execution or system shutdown.

## Business identity

Purpose: plan, rehearse, execute and verify migration of data/configuration/workflows from one software system to another with mappings, incremental sync, reconciliation and rollback.

Problem: migrations fail because hidden dependencies, dirty data, schema mismatch, missing attachments, identity ambiguity and cutover timing are discovered late.

Value: evidence-backed discovery, repeatable dry runs, explicit mapping/conflict decisions, lower downtime and provable source-to-target reconciliation.

## Complete product tree

Source/Target Discovery; Schema Profiler; Mapping Designer; Transformation Engine; Data Cleanup; Entity Resolution; Dependency Graph; Attachment/File Migrator; Permission/Identity Mapper; Configuration Migrator; Workflow/Automation Mapper; Dry-Run Sandbox; Validation/Reconciliation; Incremental/CDC Sync; Cutover Planner; Rollback Planner; Exception Workbench; Migration Evidence Pack; Connector SDK; Migration Template Marketplace; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Managed Migration Service; Vertical/System Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: source/target versions, object types, field schemas, IDs, relationships, reference data, permissions, files, comments/history, mappings, transformations, defaults, invalid records, duplicates, conflicts, incremental cursors, checkpoints, counts/hashes, sampling, business-rule tests, downtime window, cutover/rollback state and evidence.

Customers: SaaS vendors, enterprises, agencies/integrators, MSPs, consultants, IT departments, acquisitions/consolidations, platform vendors and customers switching business software.

Verticals: CRM, ERP/accounting, helpdesk, project management, HRIS, ecommerce, CMS, data warehouses, collaboration, field service, industry SaaS. Each needs source/target-specific semantic mapping packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may infer candidate mappings, explain schema semantics, identify likely dependencies and propose transformations. Deterministic migration plans, constraints, validation and reconciliation own execution. Brain cannot silently choose destructive conflict resolution or cutover.

Architecture: connector registry, source snapshot/profiling, canonical intermediate model where useful, mapping DSL, transform engine, entity resolver, dependency DAG, checkpoint/idempotency system, incremental sync, validation/reconciliation, artifact storage, protected cutover/rollback gates and audit/provenance.

## Agent tree

Discovery Agent; Schema Analyst; Mapping Agent; Data Cleanup Agent; Entity Resolution Agent; Dependency Agent; Transformation Agent; File/Attachment Agent; Permission Agent; Dry-Run Coordinator; Incremental Sync Agent; Validation/Reconciliation Agent; Cutover Planner; Rollback Coordinator; Migration QA Agent.

## Deterministic services

Connector framework; schema introspection; mapping compiler; transform functions; dependency ordering; checkpointing; idempotent writes; cursor/CDC tracking; count/hash reconciliation; referential-integrity checks; quarantine/error queues; backup/export; rollback manifests.

## Workflow tree

Authorize migration planning → discover source/target → snapshot/profiling → map schemas/entities/permissions/files → clean/transform rules → dry run → validate counts/relations/business rules → resolve exceptions → repeat until acceptance → start incremental sync → freeze/cutover window → final delta → protected cutover → verify target/source reconciliation → rollback if gates fail → close with evidence.

## Integrations / API / data

Source/target SaaS APIs, databases, file/object stores, identity/IAM, webhooks, ETL, queues, export/import formats, audit/log systems. APIs for connectors, schemas, mappings, dry runs, errors, sync state, reconciliation and cutover evidence.

Data: source snapshots/metadata, mappings, transformations, identity maps, checkpoints, errors, reconciliation results, cutover/rollback plans and evidence. Customer data is highly isolated and retained minimally.

## Monetization / distribution

Per migration, records/objects, connectors, data volume, source-target pair, seats, managed migration, enterprise/private, API/SDK and certified migration packs. Distribution via SaaS vendors, marketplaces, agencies/integrators and MSPs.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Credentials scoped to source/target, read-only discovery by default, encrypted staging, tenant isolation, PII classification, no cross-customer training, signed migration plans, protected writes/cutover, full audit and deletion of temporary copies according to retention policy.

## Failure / edge cases

API limits, source changes during migration, deleted source records, target uniqueness constraints, missing relationships, attachments too large, unsupported history, permission model mismatch, timezone/encoding issues, duplicate identities, partial cutover, webhook races, rollback after target writes. Every unsupported field/object remains explicit.

## Scale / overlap

One-off SaaS migrations → repeatable connector marketplace → enterprise migration control plane. Overlap #20 data cleanup, #42 legacy browser worker, #100 legacy modernization. #060 moves state/data/config; #100 changes the software itself.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** connector contracts, staging/provenance, versioned mappings, idempotency/checkpoints, conflict/reconciliation, protected cutover/rollback.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center data portability/recovery/provider abstractions already need these seams; reverse-map should preserve them.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** connector SDK, mapping DSL, staging isolation, dry-run/reconciliation framework.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** specific source-target connectors, migration packs, customer UI/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** massive connector marketplace and distributed migration execution.
